children.translated_text: <s>Vivekacūḍāmaṇi</s> (The Crest-Jewel of Discrimination)
who is supreme bliss, the true <s>Guru</s>. // 1 //
I bow to <s>Govinda</s>, who is the goal of all <s>Vedānta</s> conclusions, yet beyond the reach [of the senses],

children.text: jantūnāṃ narajanma durlabhamataḥ puṃstvaṃ tato vipratā

children.translated_text: beyond that, devotion to the path of Vedic <s>dharma</s>; and beyond that, learning;
discrimination between <s>Ātman</s> (Self) and non-Self, direct experience, and abiding as <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: muktir no śata-janma-koṭi-sukṛtaiḥ puṇyair vinā labhyate // 2 //
children.translated_text: liberation is not obtained without merit acquired over hundreds of millions of births. // 2 //
Among beings, human birth is difficult to obtain; even more so is manhood; rarer still is being a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
human birth, the desire for liberation, and the refuge of a great soul. // 3 //
These three things alone are rare and come about by the grace of the gods:
and moreover manhood and insight into the scriptures,
he who does not strive for the liberation of the Self is deluded in mind;
he is indeed a slayer of the Self, destroying himself through attachment to the unreal. // 4 //
Having somehow obtained the rare human birth,

children.text: itaḥ ko nvasti mūḍhātmā yas tu svārthe pramādyati &
durlabhaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ prāpya tatrāpi pauruṣam // 5 //
children.translated_text: having obtained the rare human body and moreover manhood? // 5 //
Who indeed is more foolish than the one who is negligent about his own highest good,
let them perform rituals, let them adore the deities —
without the knowledge of the oneness of the Self,
liberation is not achieved even in a hundred lifetimes of <s>Brahmā</s>. // 6 //
Let them recite the scriptures, let them worship the gods,

children.text: amṛtatvasya nāśāsti vittenety eva hi śrutiḥ &

children.translated_text: clearly declares that action is not the cause of liberation. // 7 //
'There is no hope of immortality through wealth' — thus indeed the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture)
having renounced the desire for external pleasures,
having approached a great and peaceful teacher,
with a mind concentrated on the truth taught by him. // 8 //
Therefore, for liberation, let the wise one strive,
having attained the state of being established in <s>Yoga</s>, through steadfastness in right vision. // 9 //
One should lift oneself by oneself from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
let the wise and steadfast ones strive, being devoted to the practice of the Self. // 10 //
For release from the bonds of worldly existence, having renounced all actions,

children.text: cittasya śuddhaye karma na tu vastūpalabdhaye &

children.translated_text: the realization of Reality is through inquiry, not by millions of actions. // 11 //
Action is for the purification of the mind, not for the attainment of Reality;
which destroys the fear and suffering arising from the great serpent imagined through delusion. // 12 //
Through right inquiry, the ascertainment of the true nature of the rope is achieved,

children.text: na snānena na dānena prāṇāyamaśatena vā // 13 //
children.translated_text: not through bathing, nor through charity, nor through hundreds of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) practices. // 13 //
The ascertainment of the truth of a thing is seen through inquiry into beneficial teachings,
means such as place and time are auxiliary aids in this. // 14 //
The attainment of the result especially requires a qualified person;
having approached a <s>Guru</s> who is an ocean of compassion and foremost among knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. // 15 //
Therefore, inquiry should be undertaken by one who desires to know the nature of the Self,
is qualified for Self-knowledge, being characterized by the marks stated [below]. // 16 //
An intelligent person, learned, skilled in reasoning and refutation,
the fitness for the inquiry into <s>Brahman</s> is acknowledged to belong only to the seeker of liberation. // 17 //
For one who discriminates, who is dispassionate, and who possesses the virtues of <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the rest,

children.text: yeṣu satsv eva sanniṣṭhā yadabhāve na sidhyati // 18 //
children.translated_text: only when these are present does firm devotion arise; in their absence it is not attained. // 18 //
Here, four means have been stated by the wise;
First is understood the discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal;
next, dispassion toward the enjoyment of fruits here and hereafter;
the group of six virtues beginning with <s>śama</s> (tranquility), and the desire for liberation — this is clearly [the fourfold qualification]. // 19 //
is called the discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal. // 20 //
<s>Brahman</s> is real, the world is illusory — such a firm conviction
all objects of enjoyment that are non-eternal, from the body up to <s>Brahmā</s>. // 21 //
That <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) is the desire to abandon, through seeing and hearing and such,
the steady abidance of the mind in its own goal is called <s>śama</s> (tranquility). // 22 //
Having turned away from the multitude of sense objects through the repeated perception of their defects,
Having turned away from sense objects and placing each
of the two sets of sense organs in its own sphere — that is declared as <s>dama</s> (self-restraint);
the supreme <s>uparati</s> (cessation) is the non-dependence of the mental activity on external objects. // 23 //
without anxiety and lamentation — that is called <s>titikṣā</s> (forbearance). // 24 //
The endurance of all sufferings without counter-measures,
that is called <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) by the wise, through which Reality is apprehended. // 25 //
The conviction with true understanding in the scripture and the words of the <s>Guru</s> —

children.text: sarvadā sthāpanaṃ buddheḥ śuddhe brahmaṇi sarvadā &

children.translated_text: is called <s>samādhāna</s> (concentration), not the mere entertainment of the mind. // 26 //
The constant fixing of the intellect always on pure <s>Brahman</s>
which are imagined through ignorance, through the knowledge of one's own true nature — that is <s>mumukṣutā</s> (desire for liberation). // 27 //
The desire to free oneself from the bonds beginning with ego and ending with the body,

children.text: prasādena guroḥ seyaṃ pravṛddhā sūyate phalam // 28 //
children.translated_text: and through the grace of the <s>Guru</s>, grows and bears fruit. // 28 //
Even if of mild or moderate degree, this [desire for liberation], through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the rest,

children.text: vairāgyaṃ ca mumukṣutvaṃ tīvraṃ yasya tu vidyate &

children.translated_text: <s>śama</s> (tranquility) and the other [virtues] become meaningful and fruitful. // 29 //
In one in whom <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and the desire for liberation are intense,
there <s>śama</s> and the rest are merely a semblance, like water in a desert. // 30 //
Where these two — dispassion and the desire for liberation — are weak,
the continuous inquiry into one's own true nature is called <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). // 31 //
Among the means to liberation, <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) is the greatest;
Others say that <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) is the inquiry into the reality of one's own Self;
one who possesses the said qualifications and desires to know the truth of the Self
should approach a wise <s>Guru</s>, from whom comes release from bondage. // 32 //
He who is learned in the scriptures, sinless, uncorrupted by desire, a supreme knower of <s>Brahman</s>,
who is absorbed in <s>Brahman</s>, peaceful, like a fire with its fuel exhausted,
an ocean of causeless compassion, a friend of the virtuous who bow before him. // 33 //
when he is pleased, one should ask what one needs to know about the Self. // 34 //
Having worshipped that <s>Guru</s> with devotion, through humble submission and service,
O ocean of compassion — fallen into the ocean of worldly existence,
uplift me with the glance of your gracious eye,
with a direct shower of the nectar of supreme compassion! // 35 //
O Master, salutations to you, friend of those who bow before you,
tossed about by the winds of adverse fate,
frightened, I have taken refuge — protect me from death;
I know no other shelter, O Refuge! // 36 //
Scorched by the irresistible forest fire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
like spring, bringing welfare to the world;
having themselves crossed the terrible ocean of existence,
they help others cross as well, without any motive. // 37 //
Peaceful, great, the saintly ones dwell,
their inclination to remove the suffering of others;
just as the moon of its own accord
soothes the earth scorched by the harsh rays of the sun. // 38 //
This is the nature, spontaneous indeed, of great souls —
enriched by the experience of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>, full and cooling;
for I am tormented, O Lord, by the flames of the forest fire of worldly existence —
blessed are those who are made worthy recipients of even a momentary glance from you! // 39 //
Sprinkle me with your words of nectar, pleasing to the ear, poured from the vessel of your speech,
What is my destiny? What means is there?
I know nothing — have mercy on me, O Lord,
and alleviate the affliction of the sorrow of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 40 //
How shall I cross this ocean of worldly existence?
scorched by the heat of the forest fire of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
gazing upon him with a look moist with the essence of compassion,
the great soul instantly grants him freedom from fear. // 41 //
Seeing the one who speaks thus, who has taken refuge,
who is a seeker of liberation, who acts according to what is prescribed,
whose mind is tranquil and endowed with <s>śama</s> (tranquility),
should impart the teaching of the truth. // 42 //
The wise one, out of compassion alone, to that student who has approached him,
there is a means to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
by the very path by which the ascetics have reached the other shore,
that same path I point out to you. // 43 //
Fear not, O learned one, there is no danger for you;
by that, having crossed the ocean of worldly existence, you shall attain supreme bliss. // 44 //
There is a certain great means that destroys the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
by that, the complete destruction of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> subsequently takes place. // 45 //
Through inquiry into the meaning of <s>Vedānta</s>, the highest knowledge arises;
are declared by the voice of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) directly as the causes of liberation;
whoever abides in these very [practices] —
for him there is liberation from the bondage of the body imagined through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // 46 //
For the seeker of liberation — faith, devotion, meditation, and <s>Yoga</s>
and from that indeed comes <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration);
the fire of knowledge born from the discrimination between the two
burns up the effects of ignorance together with their root. // 47 //
Through the conjunction with <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), the bondage of the non-Self upon the Supreme Self is yours,
The disciple said:

children.text: kṛpayā śrūyatāṃ svāmin praśno 'yaṃ kriyate mayā &

children.translated_text: having heard the answer to which from your lips, I shall be fulfilled. // 48 //
Out of compassion, may this question asked by me be heard, O Master;

children.text: ko nāma bandhaḥ katham eṣa āgataḥ

children.translated_text: How does it persist? How is there liberation from it?
What is the non-Self? What is the Supreme Self?
How is the discrimination between them? Please explain this. // 49 //
What indeed is bondage? How has it come about?
The blessed <s>Guru</s> said:

children.text: dhanyo 'si kṛtakṛtyo 'si pāvita te kulaṃ tvayā &

children.translated_text: for you desire to become <s>Brahman</s> by freeing yourself from the bondage of ignorance. // 50 //
Blessed are you, your purpose is fulfilled, your family is purified by you,
but no one other than oneself can free one from bondage. // 51 //
Sons and others can free a father from debt,

children.text: kṣudhādikṛtaduḥkhaṃ tu vinā svena na kenacit // 52 //
children.translated_text: but the suffering caused by hunger and such can be removed by none other than oneself. // 52 //
The suffering of a burden placed on one's head can be relieved by others,
he alone attains health, not through the actions performed by another. // 53 //
A sick person who follows the proper diet and medicine —
through the eye of clear understanding, not through a scholar;
the form of the moon is to be known by one's own eyes alone —
can it be known through others? // 54 //
The true nature of a thing is to be known by oneself alone
who is able without the Self, even in hundreds of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (ages)? // 55 //
To untie the bonds of ignorance, desire, and action —

children.text: na yogena na sāṃkhyena karmaṇā no na vidyayā &

children.translated_text: liberation is attained only through the knowledge of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s>, not otherwise. // 56 //
Neither by <s>Yoga</s>, nor by <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, nor by action, nor by learning —
merely delight the people; they do not serve to gain sovereignty. // 57 //
The beauty of the <s>vīṇā</s>'s form and the skill of playing its strings

children.text: vaiduṣyaṃ viduṣāṃ tadvadbhuktaye na tu muktaye // 58 //
children.translated_text: the erudition of the learned is likewise for enjoyment, not for liberation. // 58 //
Eloquence of speech, a torrent of words, and skill in expounding scriptures —
even when the Supreme Truth is known, the study of scriptures is fruitless. // 59 //
When the Supreme Truth is not known, the study of scriptures is fruitless;
therefore, the truth of the Self must be known with effort by those who know Reality. // 60 //
The jungle of words is a great forest that causes the mind to wander;

children.text: kimu vedaiśca śāstraiśca kimu mantraiḥ kimauṣadhaiḥ // 61 //
children.translated_text: of what use are the <s>Vedas</s> and scriptures? Of what use are <s>mantras</s>? Of what use are medicines? // 61 //
For one bitten by the serpent of ignorance, without the medicine of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>,
without direct experience, one is not liberated by merely uttering the word '<s>Brahman</s>'. // 62 //
A disease does not go away by merely uttering the name of medicine without drinking it;
how can there be liberation for people through mere words about <s>Brahman</s>, which yield nothing but verbal results? // 63 //
Without dissolving the phenomenal world and without knowing the truth of the Self,
one cannot become a king merely by saying 'I am a king'. // 64 //
Without destroying the enemy and without gaining the wealth of the entire earth,

children.text: nikṣepaḥ samapekṣate nahi bahiḥ śabdaistu nirgacchati &
children.translated_text: these are what a treasure requires; it does not come forth by mere words;
likewise, the pure truth of oneself, hidden by the effects of <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), is attained through the teaching of a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, reflection, meditation, and such,
not through false reasoning. // 65 //
The authoritative statement, the digging, the removal of stones and such above, the taking possession —

children.text: svair eva yatnaḥ kartavyo rogādāv iva paṇḍitaiḥ // 66 //
children.translated_text: the wise should make their own exertion, as in the case of disease and such. // 66 //
Therefore, for liberation from the bonds of worldly existence, with every effort,
it is concise like a <s>sūtra</s>, profound in meaning, and should be known by seekers of liberation. // 67 //
This question raised by you today is excellent and approved by those versed in scriptures;
by hearing this, you shall immediately be freed from the bonds of worldly existence. // 68 //
Listen attentively, O learned one, to what is declared by me;
complete <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) toward all non-eternal things;
then <s>śama</s> (tranquility), and also <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), <s>titikṣā</s> (forbearance),
and the thorough renunciation of all actions done with attachment. // 69 //
The first cause of liberation is declared to be
and prolonged, constant, uninterrupted meditation on the truth by the sage;
then the wise one, transcending to the unconditioned state
The bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) is attained right here [in this life]. // 70 //
Then listening to the scriptures, reflection upon them,
This I shall properly expound to you; having heard it, ascertain it within yourself. // 71 //
What is to be known by you now is the discrimination of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) from the non-Self.
And skin —
Furnished with legs, thighs, chest, arms, back, and head
As limbs and sub-limbs — this [is the body]. // 72 //
Composed of the seven constituents — marrow, bone, fat, flesh, blood, dermis,
The abode of delusion, is called 'gross' by the wise.
Space, air, fire, water, and earth —
These are the subtle elements. // 73 //
This body, well-known through the notions of 'I' and 'mine,'
They become gross and are the causes of the gross body.
Their properties become the sense-objects —
The five, beginning with sound, exist for the enjoyment of the experiencer. // 74 //
Having combined with portions of each other,
By the terrible rope of attachment, so difficult to restrain,
Go up and down, high and low,
Led swiftly by the messenger of their own <s>karma</s>. // 75 //
Those who are deluded and bound to these sense-objects
Met their death, each bound by its own [particular] quality —
The deer, the elephant, the moth, the fish,
And the bee — what then of a person afflicted by all five? // 76 //
By the five [objects] beginning with sound, five alone
Poison kills only the one who ingests it, but a sense-object kills even one who merely beholds it with the eyes. // 77 //
A sense-object is more virulent in its harm than the venom of a black cobra;

children.text: sa eva kalpate muktyai nānyaḥ ṣaṭśāstravedy api // 78 //
children.translated_text: Is fit for liberation — no other, even if he knows the six <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures). // 78 //
He alone who is freed from the great noose of desire for sense-objects, so difficult to renounce,
And set out to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) —
The shark of desire drags them down midway,
Seizing them by the throat and forcibly pulling them back. // 79 //
Those seekers of liberation who possess only superficial dispassion
Crosses to the far shore of the ocean of existence, free from obstacles. // 80 //
He who has slain the shark called sense-objects with the sword of supreme dispassion
Death approaches at every step.
But for one who walks by the instruction of a beneficent teacher and <s>guru</s>, through his own discernment,

children.text: prabhavati phalasiddhiḥ satyam ity eva viddhi // 81 //
children.translated_text: The fruition of the goal truly arises — know this for certain. // 81 //
Know that for one of impure intellect who walks the treacherous paths of sense-objects,
Abandon sense-objects far away, as you would poison.
Cultivate always with care contentment, which is like nectar, compassion, straightforwardness,
Tranquility, and self-restraint. // 82 //
If indeed you have a desire for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),
Of liberating oneself from the bondage created by beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
And is attached to nourishing this body, which exists for another's purpose —
He kills himself by his own hand. // 83 //
One who neglects at every moment the duty

children.text: grāhaṃ dārudhiyā dhṛtvā nadi tartuṃ sa gacchati // 84 //
children.translated_text: Is like one who crosses a river holding onto a crocodile, thinking it to be a log. // 84 //
He who desires to nourish his body while wishing to know the <s>Ātman</s> (Self)
He who has conquered delusion deserves the state of liberation. // 85 //
Delusion itself is the great death for the seeker of liberation, in regard to the body and such things.

children.text: yaṃ jitvā munayo yānti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // 86 //
children.translated_text: Conquering which, the sages go to that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // 86 //
Conquer delusion, the great death, regarding the body, wife, children, and the like —
Full of urine and excrement — this gross body is contemptible. // 87 //
Filled with skin, flesh, blood, sinews, fat, marrow, and bones,
From the gross elements that have undergone <s>pañcīkaraṇa</s> (quintuplication), by virtue of past <s>karma</s>,
This gross body is produced — the dwelling place of experience for the Self.
Its state of waking is that in which the experience of gross objects occurs. // 88 //
Of various forms — garlands, sandalwood, women, and so forth —
Is undertaken by the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) of its own accord.
Therefore, the eminence of this body is in the waking state. // 89 //
Through the external sense organs, the enjoyment of gross objects
Is like a house for the householder. // 90 //
Know that this gross body, upon which depends all external worldly existence of the person,
Corpulence and the like, and the various states beginning with childhood, are its conditions.
The regulations of <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), and manifold afflictions,
And the distinctions such as honor, dishonor, and respect, are its characteristics. // 91 //
Birth, old age, and death are the properties of the gross body;
Nose, and tongue — so called because of their apprehension of sense-objects.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and the organ of generation
Are the <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (organs of action), due to their inclination toward action. // 92 //
The <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (organs of knowledge) are the ear, skin, eye,
<s>Ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego), and <s>citta</s> (thought) — according to their respective functions.
<s>Manas</s> (mind) is so called from its functions of willing and doubting;
<s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) from its nature of determining the meaning of objects. // 93 //
The inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) is called <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect),
<s>Citta</s> (thought) is so called from its quality of attending to its own interests. // 94 //
<s>Ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego) is so called from the sense of self-identification as 'I.'
It is one entity itself, but differs according to its different functions and modifications, like gold, water, and the like. // 95 //
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s> — that is the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);
The five beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>, the five beginning with space (ether),
<s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) too, and desire and <s>karma</s> (action) —
These eight constituents are called the <s>sūkṣma-śarīra</s> (subtle body). // 96 //
The five [organs] beginning with speech, the five beginning with hearing,
Also known as the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s>, born of the un-quintupled [elements].
It is the experiencer of the fruits of <s>karma</s>, endowed with latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>),
And is the beginningless limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) of the <s>Ātman</s>, due to its own ignorance. // 97 //
Hear about this body called the subtle body,
In which it shines forth with the residue of its own [impressions] alone.

children.text: svapne tu buddhiḥ svayam eva jāgrat
children.translated_text: In dream, the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) itself, of its own accord,
Manifests through the manifold latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) from the waking state. // 98 //
Dream is the distinctive state of this [subtle body],

children.text:
kartrādibhāvaṃ pratipadya rājate
  yatra svayaṃ bhāti hyayaṃ parātmā &
dhīmātrakopādhiraśeṣasākṣī

children.translated_text: It is not stained even by a trace of the actions performed by that [intellect].
Since it is unattached, therefore by actions
Performed by the limiting adjunct, it is not stained in the least. // 99 //
Where it shines forth, assuming the roles of agent and so on — there the supreme Self itself shines. Being a mere witness, with intellect alone as its limiting adjunct,
Just as an axe and the like are instruments of the carpenter. Therefore, this Self is unattached. // 100 //
This <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) is the instrument of all the activities of the conscious Self, the <s>puruṣa</s>,
Of the eye, due to its good or bad condition.
Likewise, deafness, muteness, and the like
Are properties of the ear and other organs — not of the knower, the <s>Ātman</s>. // 101 //
Blindness, dullness, and sharpness are properties
Secretion, and departure [of the vital breath] — such are the activities
That the knowers declare to be the functions of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath).
Hunger and thirst are also properties of <s>prāṇa</s>. // 102 //
Inhalation, exhalation, yawning, sneezing,
Abides with the sense of 'I,' through the light of reflected [consciousness]. // 103 //
The inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), amidst these [organs] such as the eye, and in the body,
Through association with the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>sattva</s> and others, it undergoes the three states. // 104 //
This should be known as the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) — the agent, the enjoyer, the one who identifies.

children.text: sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca taddharmaḥ sadānandasya nātmanaḥ // 105 //
children.translated_text: Happiness and unhappiness are its properties — not of the <s>Ātman</s>, which is ever blissful. // 105 //
It is happy when sense-objects are favorable, and unhappy when they are unfavorable.

children.text: ātmārthatvena hi preyānviṣayo na svataḥ priyaḥ &
children.translated_text: Sense-objects are dear for the sake of the Self; the sense-object is not dear in itself.

children.text: svata eva hi sarveṣāmātmā priyatamo yataḥ \
children.translated_text: Since the Self is the dearest of all to everyone,

children.text: tata ātmā sadānando nāsya duḥkhaṃ kadācana // 106 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the Self is ever blissful; sorrow never belongs to it. // 106 //
Is attested by scripture, direct perception, tradition, and inference in the waking state. // 107 //
That bliss of the Self which is experienced in deep sleep, free from objects,
Beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, transcendent —
Inferable only from its effects, by the wise alone [recognized as] <s>māyā</s> —
By which all this universe is brought forth. // 108 //

observing all these — the ego-mind and the like, which are participants in modifications of various forms —

children.text: nityānandacid ātmanā sphurati taṃ viddhi svametaṃ hṛdi // 217 //
children.translated_text: it shines as the eternal bliss-consciousness Self; know this as your own Self in the heart. // 217 //
That which manifests most clearly in waking, dream, and deep sleep,
a fool takes it to be the sun itself;
just so, the dull person, through delusion, identifies with 'I'
the reflection of consciousness situated in the limiting adjuncts. // 218 //
Seeing the reflection of the sun's disc in the water of a pot,
all of these — the sun itself is perceived;
standing apart, illuminating all three,
self-luminous — just so does the wise person [perceive the Self]. // 219 //
Setting aside the pot, the water, and the reflection of the sun therein —
thus deposited in the cave of the intellect,
the Seer, the <s>Ātman</s>, of undivided awareness,
the illuminator of all, distinct from both the existent and the non-existent, // 220 //
Setting aside the body, the intellect, and the reflection of consciousness
void of interior and exterior, having no other than itself —
knowing correctly this as one's own true nature,
a person becomes free from sin, free from impurity, free from death. // 221 //
eternal, all-pervading, omnipresent, supremely subtle,
one fears nothing from anywhere whatsoever;
there is no other path to liberation from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence)
for the seeker of liberation, other than the realization of one's own true nature. // 222 //
Free from sorrow, a mass of bliss, wise,
by which the wise attain non-dual, blissful <s>Brahman</s>. // 223 //
The knowledge of non-difference from <s>Brahman</s> is the cause of liberation from worldly existence,
therefore, the non-difference of the Self from <s>Brahman</s> must be properly known. // 224 //
One who has become <s>Brahman</s> does not return again to <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);

children.text: satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma viśuddhaṃ paraṃ svataḥsiddham &

children.translated_text: of the one essence of eternal bliss, non-different from the inner Self, uninterrupted — it triumphs! // 225 //
<s>Brahman</s> is truth, knowledge, infinite, pure, supreme, self-established,
indeed, there is nothing else whatsoever in the state of the realization of the supreme ultimate truth. // 226 //
This reality is the supreme non-dual (<s>Advaita</s>), since no other object exists apart from itself;
all that is <s>Brahman</s> alone, once the defect of all false notions has been eliminated. // 227 //
This entire universe of manifold forms, perceived due to ignorance —
it exists everywhere as clay in its essential nature;
the form of the pot does not exist separately — the pot
is merely a falsely imagined name, nothing more. // 228 //
A pot, though an effect of clay, is not different from clay;
be shown as something different from clay;
therefore, the pot is merely imagined through delusion —
clay alone is real, the ultimate reality. // 229 //
By no one can the essential nature of the pot
there is nothing other than That;

children.text: astīti yo vakti na tasya moho
children.translated_text: whoever says 'it exists' [as something separate] — their delusion
has not departed; it is like the babbling of one asleep. // 230 //
Everything that is an effect of real <s>Brahman</s> is real, being That alone;
the most excellent <s>Śruti</s> (scripture), established in the <s>Atharva Veda</s>;
therefore, this universe is nothing but <s>Brahman</s>,
for what is superimposed is not different from its substratum. // 231 //
'This universe is <s>Brahman</s> alone' — thus speaks
there would be the loss of the infinity of the Self, the scriptures would become invalid,
and the Lord would become a speaker of falsehood —
none of these three is fitting or beneficial for great souls. // 232 //
If this world were real in terms of the <s>Ātman</s>,

children.text: na ca matsthāni bhūtānīty evam eva vyacīkḷpat // 233 //
children.translated_text: nor do beings abide in Me' — thus He has indeed declared. // 233 //
'The Lord, the knower of the true nature of things — I do not abide in them,
since nothing whatsoever is perceived [there], it is unreal and false, like a dream. // 234 //
If the world were real, it should be perceived in deep sleep;
its separate perception is false, like [the attribution of] qualities and the like;
what reality can belong to that which is superimposed?
It is the substratum alone that appears thus through error. // 235 //
Therefore, the world does not exist apart from the supreme <s>Ātman</s>;
that delusion itself is [the cause] — that silver is indeed [nothing but] the nacre;
<s>Brahman</s> is always experienced in the form of 'this' —
what is superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s> is mere name. // 236 //
Whatever is perceived by a deluded person, from the standpoint of delusion,
a mass of pure knowledge, untainted,
perfectly tranquil, without beginning or end, actionless,
of the nature of uninterrupted bliss. // 237 //
Therefore, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is existence, non-dual,
eternal, blissful, partless, immeasurable,
formless, unmanifest, nameless, indestructible,
it is a self-luminous light that shines as something [indescribable]. // 238 //
Having cast off all distinctions created by <s>Māyā</s> (illusion),
the supreme truth is known by the wise as pure, undivided consciousness alone. // 239 //
Free from knower, knowable, and knowledge; infinite; beyond all conceptual thought;
immeasurable, without beginning or end — <s>Brahman</s> is fullness, I am that great light. // 240 //
Neither to be rejected nor to be acquired; beyond the reach of mind and speech;
namely <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s>, when properly refined — if thus understood,
the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture), through the statement '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art), repeatedly
establishes their complete identity. // 241 //
Of the two terms denoted by 'That' (<s>tat</s>) and 'Thou' (<s>tvam</s>),
since they possess mutually contradictory attributes —
like the firefly and the sun, the king and the servant,
the well and the ocean, the atom and the mountain. // 242 //
The identity of those two is stated in their implied senses, not in their literal senses,
and is not real in any way; these limiting adjuncts are:
<s>Māyā</s> (illusion), the cause of the great [cosmic elements] and the like, for <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord),
and the five sheaths as the effect, for the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) — hear this! // 243 //
The contradiction between them is created by the limiting adjuncts
when they are properly negated, there is neither the supreme nor the individual —
the kingdom belongs to the king, the shield to the soldier;

children.text: tayor apohe na bhaṭo na rājā // 244 //
children.translated_text: when both are removed, there is neither soldier nor king. // 244 //
These are the two limiting adjuncts of the supreme and the individual;
negates the duality superimposed upon <s>Brahman</s>;
through understanding supported by the authority of <s>Śruti</s>,
the negation of both must indeed be undertaken. // 245 //
'Now then, the teaching...' — the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) itself
like a snake seen in a rope, or like a dream;
thus, having properly negated the seen through reasoning,
one should know the oneness that exists between those two. // 246 //
'Not this, not this' — being imagined, it is not real,
for the establishment of their undivided, unitary essence;
neither exclusive indication nor non-exclusive indication suffices,
but rather one must contemplate through indication that partakes of both meanings. // 247 //
Then, those two are well indicated through implication,
by setting aside the contradictory aspects;
just so, in the statement '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art),
having abandoned the contradictory attributes in both, // 248 //
'That is this <s>Devadatta</s>' — here identity is stated
the undivided nature is ascertained by the wise;
thus, through hundreds of great statements,
the identity and undivided nature of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s> is declared. // 249 //
by recognizing both as pure consciousness, the real Self,

children.text:
asthūlamityetadasannirasya
  siddhaṃ svato vyomavadapratarkyam &
ato mṛṣāmātramidaṃ pratītaṃ

children.translated_text: abandon what has been grasped as the Self [falsely];
with the purified understanding 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,'
know your own Self as undivided awareness. // 250 //
'Not gross' and such [descriptions] — by negating the unreal, the Self-established, like space, beyond reasoning — is proven; therefore, all this perceived [world] is mere illusion;
just so, all that is born of Being (<s>Sat</s>) is nothing but Being alone, in its entirety;

children.text: yasmānnāsti sataḥ paraṃ kim api tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā svayaṃ
children.translated_text: since there is nothing whatsoever beyond Being — that is the truth, that is the <s>Ātman</s>, that is oneself;
therefore, '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — the tranquil, pure, non-dual, supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 251 //
All effects of clay, such as pots and the like, are always nothing but clay;
false, so too in waking, the world [is false] because it is a product of one's own ignorance;
since thus this body, the senses, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), the ego, and the like are all unreal,
therefore, '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — the tranquil, pure, non-dual, supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 252 //
Just as space, time, objects, and the knower imagined in sleep are all
that alone remains and is not different from it;
when a dream is dissolved, has the variegated dream-world
ever been seen as something different from oneself upon awakening? // 253 //
Where something is imagined through delusion, upon discrimination
devoid of name, form, quality, and defect,
transcending space, time, and objects —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — contemplate this in the Self. // 254 //
Beyond caste, custom, family, and lineage,
yet within the range of the eye of pure awareness,
that which is pure, condensed consciousness, the beginningless reality —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; '<s>Tat tvam asi</s>' (That thou art) — contemplate this in the Self. // 255 //
That supreme [reality], beyond the range of all speech,
not apprehended by the senses,
That which is unknowable by the intellect, that which is blameless —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 256 //
Untouched by the six waves [of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, old age, and death], meditated upon in the hearts of <s>yogins</s>,
which is self-supporting and distinct from both being and non-being,
which is partless, incomparable, and immeasurable — know that
to be <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 257 //
That which is the substratum of the manifold world imagined through delusion,
disease, and destruction — imperishable,
the cause of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 258 //
Free from birth, growth, maturation, decline,
still like a waveless ocean,
eternally free, of undivided form —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 259 //
Without differentiation, with characteristics that cannot be negated,
the cause that negates all other causes,
itself distinct from both cause and effect —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 260 //
The one alone that is real, the cause of the many,
that which is the supreme, distinct from both the perishable and the imperishable,
eternal, immutable bliss, untainted —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 261 //
Free from thought-constructions, not small, imperishable,
in the form of names, forms, qualities, and modifications,
yet itself always unchanging, like gold —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 262 //
That which shines as the real, appearing as manifold through delusion,
the inmost, of one essence, whose nature is the Self,
truth, consciousness, bliss, infinite, imperishable —
that is <s>Brahman</s>; 'That thou art' — meditate on this in the Self. // 263 //
That which shines as having nothing beyond it, the highest of the high,
through the intellect using well-established reasoning,
free from doubt and the like, as clear as water in the palm of the hand —
thereby the ascertainment of the truth will come about. // 264 //
The meaning stated here should be meditated upon in the Self by oneself,
like a king in his army, established in that support,
ever abiding in your own Self,
dissolve the world-born [appearances] in <s>Brahman</s>. // 265 //
Having realized the pure truth which is consciousness alone,
<s>Brahman</s> exists — real, supreme, without a second.
He who as the Self dwells here in that cave
has no further entry into the cave of the body. // 266 //
In the cave of the intellect, distinct from being and non-being,
the firm notion 'I am the doer, I am the enjoyer,' which is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);
this is to be removed with effort by dwelling in the Self through inward vision —
the sages call <s>mukti</s> (liberation) that which is the thinning out of <s>vāsanās</s>. // 267 //
Even when the reality is known, the beginningless and powerful <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) remains —
this superimposition should be abandoned by the wise through steadfast devotion to one's own Self. // 268 //
The notion 'I' and 'mine' regarding the body, senses, and so on, which are not the Self —
through the true disposition 'I am That,' abandon the notion of Self in what is not the Self. // 269 //
Having known one's own inner Self as the witness of the intellect and its modifications,
abandoning conformity to the scriptures — remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 270 //
Abandoning conformity to the world, abandoning conformity to the body,
for the body, knowledge of a being does not arise as it should. // 271 //
Due to <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) for the world, for scriptures, and
the threefold <s>vāsanā</s> is like an iron shackle binding the feet —
those who know say this firmly;
he who is freed from it attains liberation. // 272 //
For one who desires liberation from the prison of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
arising from contact with water and such,
clearly manifests again through rubbing,
when the external odor is properly removed. // 273 //
The divine fragrance of <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood), overwhelmed by a foul smell
of the endless <s>vāsanās</s> of the non-Self lurking within,
when purified by the friction of intense wisdom,
becomes clearly perceptible, like the fragrance of sandalwood. // 274 //
The supreme <s>vāsanā</s> (aspiration) of the Self, smeared over by the dust

children.text: nityātmaniṣṭhayā teṣāṃ nāśe bhāti svayaṃ sphuṭam // 275 //
children.translated_text: shines forth of itself, clearly, through the destruction of those [non-Self vāsanās] by constant devotion to the eternal Self. // 275 //
The <s>vāsanā</s> of the Self, concealed by the web of non-Self <s>vāsanās</s>,
to that extent it relinquishes external <s>vāsanās</s>;
when <s>vāsanās</s> are completely exhausted,
the experience of the Self becomes free from obstruction. // 276 //
To the extent that the mind becomes established in the inner Self,

children.text: svātmany eva sadā sthitvā mano naśyati yoginaḥ &

children.translated_text: and thereby the <s>vāsanās</s> are destroyed; therefore, remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 277 //
By ever abiding in one's own Self, the <s>yogin's</s> mind perishes,

children.text: tamo dvābhyāṃ rajaḥ sattvātsattvaṃ śuddhena naśyati &

children.translated_text: therefore, taking hold of <s>sattva</s>, remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 278 //
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness) is destroyed by the two [<s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s>], <s>rajas</s> by <s>sattva</s>, and <s>sattva</s> by pure [<s>sattva</s>];
taking hold of courage, and with effort remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 279 //
Determining that <s>prārabdha</s> (fructified karma) sustains the body, be steadfast,
remove the superimposition on your own Self, acquired through the force of <s>vāsanā</s>. // 280 //
'I am not the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), I am the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — through the prior negation of what is not That,

children.text: śrutyā yuktyā svānubhūtyā jñātvā sārvātmyam ātmanaḥ &

children.translated_text: remove the superimposition on your own Self, acquired even from the slightest appearance [of non-Self]. // 281 //
Having known the all-pervading nature of the Self through scripture, reasoning, and personal experience,
by constant single-pointed devotion to That, remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 282 //
Since there is no activity whatsoever for the sage in the form of taking up or abandoning,
for the firmness of Self-identity with <s>Brahman</s>, remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 283 //
From the knowledge of the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s> arising from the <s>mahāvākyas</s> (great statements) like 'That thou art,'
with attentive and concentrated mind, remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 284 //
Until the complete dissolution of the sense of 'I' in this body,
so long, O wise one, unceasingly remove the superimposition on your own Self. // 285 //
So long as the perception of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and the world appears like a dream,
sounds, and the like, or forgetfulness — contemplate the Self in the Self. // 286 //
Without giving even a moment's opportunity to sleep, worldly talk,
abandoning it as far as an outcaste, become <s>Brahman</s> and be fulfilled. // 287 //
This body, born from the impurity of mother and father, composed of flesh and filth —
and through the state of undivided wholeness, be forever silent, O sage. // 288 //
Just as pot-space [is dissolved] in the great space, so dissolve the Self in the Supreme Self,
abandon both the macrocosm and the microcosm like a vessel of filth. // 289 //
Having become the self-luminous ground, self-existent, with the eternal Self,
casting off the subtle body, be the absolute one forever. // 290 //
Placing the sense of 'I,' mounted upon the body, in the Self of pure consciousness, ever blissful,
knowing 'I am that <s>Brahman</s>,' you shall become one who has fulfilled all purposes. // 291 //
That in which this world-appearance [exists] like a city in a mirror —
consciousness, non-dual, bliss, formless, actionless,
one should cast off the false body assumed by oneself,
like an actor [abandoning] a costume. // 292 //
Attaining that which is truly existent, one's own primordial form,
the meaning of 'I' is not [the visible], since it is seen to be momentary.
The awareness 'I know everything' —
how could 'I' and such be established as momentary? // 293 //
All this visible [world] is utterly false in every respect;
as it is perceived even in deep sleep at all times.

children.text: brūte hyajo nitya iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) itself declares 'It is unborn and eternal' —
that inner Self is distinct from both being and non-being. // 294 //
The true meaning of 'I' is the witness of the 'I'-sense and its counterparts,
must itself be eternally free from modification.
In fantasy, dream, and deep sleep, clearly
again and again the unreality of these two [body and ego] is seen. // 295 //
The knower of all modifications of all that is subject to change
and with the identifier of the lump, which is a construction of the intellect.
Knowing your own Self as undivided awareness, unaffected by the three times,
attain peace. // 296 //
Therefore, abandon the false identification with this lump of flesh,
form, and stages of life, which pertain to the moist corpse;
abandon also the properties of the subtle body such as doership —
become the essence of undivided bliss. // 297 //
Abandon the false identification with family, lineage, name,
of these, the root and the first modification is <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego). // 298 //
There are other obstacles seen as causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> for a person;
there is not even the slightest talk of liberation, which is of a different nature. // 299 //
As long as one has any connection with the wicked <s>ahaṃkāra</s>,
pure like the moon, full, ever blissful, self-luminous. // 300 //
Freed from the grip of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, one attains one's own true nature,

children.text: yo vā pure so 'ham iti pratīto

children.translated_text: projected by the intellect deluded by dense <s>tamas</s> (darkness) —
upon the complete destruction of that very thing,
the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Ātman</s> becomes free from obstruction. // 301 //
That which was formerly apprehended as 'I am this,'
guarded by it in the Self, with three fierce heads made of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);
cutting off the three heads with the great sword called <s>vijñāna</s> (discriminative knowledge), sharpened by scripture,
and uprooting this serpent, the wise one is able to enjoy the bliss-giving treasure. // 302 //
The treasure of the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> is coiled about by the terrible serpent of <s>ahaṃkāra</s>,
how can there be health? Similarly, the sense of 'I' [obstructs] a <s>yogin's</s> liberation. // 303 //
As long as there is even the slightest trace of the poison's effect in the body,
through the discrimination of the inner truth, one realizes the reality: 'I am This.' // 304 //
Through the complete cessation of 'I'-ness and the withdrawal of the manifold thought-constructions caused by it,
which is of the nature of modification, which reflects the Self, and which robs one of one's natural state.
Through superimposition upon which, this <s>saṃsāra</s>, full of birth, death, old age, and suffering,
has come upon you — the inner one, of the form of consciousness, whose nature is bliss. // 305 //
Quickly abandon the notion 'I' in <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, the agent,
whose nature is bliss, of blameless glory —
there is no other <s>saṃsāra</s> anywhere for you who are changeless,
except through the superimposition of 'I' upon this [body-mind complex]. // 306 //
For the Self of consciousness, always of one form, all-pervading,
perceived like a thorn in the throat of the enjoyer,
having clearly cut it with the great sword of discriminative knowledge,
enjoy the bliss of the sovereignty of the Self as you please. // 307 //
Therefore, this <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, one's own enemy,
with all attachment abandoned through the attainment of the Supreme Reality,
be silent, resting in the experience of the bliss of the Self,
with the fullness of the Self, free from thought-constructions, in <s>Brahman</s>. // 308 //
Then, having turned back the activity of the 'I'-sense and such,
revived by the mind even for a moment,
it springs to life and produces hundreds of distractions,
as a cloud in the rainy season [is driven] by the wind. // 309 //
Even when the great 'I' has been cut at the root, if it is
should ever be given to it through the contemplation of sense objects;
that alone is the cause of its revival,
like water for a withered lemon tree. // 310 //
Having restrained the enemy <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, no opportunity
how can one distinct [from the body] be a desirer?
Therefore, the very pursuit of sense objects
is the cause of bondage to worldly existence through attachment to differentiation. // 311 //
One who identifies with the body alone is a desirer;
through the destruction of effects, the seed is destroyed — therefore one should restrain the effects. // 312 //
Through the increase of effects, the increase of the seed is observed;

children.text: vardhate sarvathā puṃsaḥ saṃsāro na nivartate // 313 //
children.translated_text: in every way, a person's <s>saṃsāra</s> does not cease. // 313 //
Through the growth of <s>vāsanā</s>, effects increase, and through the increase of effects, <s>vāsanā</s> grows;
<s>vāsanā</s> grows from these two: internal thought and external action. // 314 //
To sever the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the renunciant should burn both of these;

children.text: tābhyāṃ pravardhamānā sā sūte saṃsṛtim ātmanaḥ &

children.translated_text: the means of destroying all three, at all times and in all conditions, // 315 //
Increasing through those two, it produces <s>saṃsāra</s> for oneself;
through the firmness of the <s>vāsanā</s> for Reality, those three attain dissolution. // 316 //
is the perception of <s>Brahman</s> alone everywhere, in everything, and from everything;
the exhaustion of <s>vāsanā</s> is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — that is called <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living). // 317 //
Upon the destruction of action, the destruction of thought follows, and from that, the exhaustion of <s>vāsanā</s>;
the <s>vāsanā</s> of the 'I'-sense and the like, though dissolved, [may linger];
but even if greatly advanced, in the presence of the dawn's radiance,
darkness thoroughly dissolves, just as it does. // 318 //
When the <s>vāsanā</s> for the Real blossoms and expands,
are not seen when the sun of day has risen;
likewise, in the experience of non-dual bliss,

children.text: na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ // 319 //
children.translated_text: there is neither bondage nor even a trace of suffering. // 319 //
Darkness, the effects of darkness, and the web of miseries
contemplating only Being, a mass of bliss,
remain absorbed, whether outwardly or inwardly —
pass your time [thus], even while the bonds of <s>karma</s> persist. // 320 //
Dissolving the perceived visible [world],
'Negligence is death' — thus says the blessed son of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Sanatkumāra</s>). // 321 //
One should never be negligent in one's devotion to <s>Brahman</s>;
from that [negligence] comes delusion, from that the 'I'-sense, from that bondage, and from that suffering. // 322 //
There is no calamity greater than negligence for the knower, from the standpoint of one's own true nature;

children.text: vikṣepayati dhīdoṣair yoṣā jāram iva priyam // 323 //
children.translated_text: distracts the intellect through its defects, as a woman diverts her lover. // 323 //
Even a wise person, seeing the mind directed toward sense objects, is [overcome by] forgetfulness;

children.text: āvṛṇoti tathā māyā prājñaṃ vāpi parāṅmukham // 324 //
children.translated_text: but covers [the water] again, so <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) covers even the wise one who turns away. // 324 //
Just as moss that is pushed aside does not stay away for even a moment
were to fall outward, it would tumble here and there,
like a ball dropped through carelessness
falling down a flight of stairs. // 325 //
If the mind, even slightly slipping from the goal,
from thorough imagination arises desire, and from desire, a person's activity. // 326 //
When the mind enters into sense objects, it imagines their qualities;
in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption);
one who is concentrated attains perfection completely —
be concentrated in mind, be vigilant! // 327 //
