children.text: yasya cittaṃ viniścintaṃ sa jīvanmukta iṣyate // 430 //
children.translated_text: whose mind is free from anxiety — that one is regarded as <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 430 //
One in whom the agitations of <s>saṃsāra</s> are stilled, who, though possessing faculties, is without parts,
the absence of the sense of 'I' and 'mine' is the mark of the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 431 //
Even while this body persists, following one like a shadow,
and having attained indifference [to the present] — this is the mark of the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 432 //
Not dwelling on the past, not deliberating on the future,
equal vision everywhere — this is the mark of the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 433 //
In this world distinguished by virtues and faults, inherently diverse,
remaining unchanged in both cases — this is the mark of the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 434 //
When desired and undesired things are encountered, with equal vision in the Self,
not perceiving inner or outer — this is the mark of the <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 435 //
With the mind absorbed in savoring the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>,
one who stands in indifference — that one bears the mark of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living). // 436 //
Free from the sense of 'mine' and 'I' regarding the body, senses, and the like, and their duties,
freed from the bonds of worldly existence — that one bears the mark of <s>jīvanmukti</s>. // 437 //
One who has known the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of the Self by the strength of <s>Śruti</s> (scripture),

children.text: yasya no bhavataḥ kvāpi sa jīvanmukta iṣyate // 438 //
children.translated_text: one in whom these never arise anywhere — that one is regarded as <s>jīvanmukta</s>. // 438 //
The sense of 'I' in the body and senses, and the sense of 'this' in other things —
nor between <s>Brahman</s> and the creation — that one bears the mark of <s>jīvanmukti</s>. // 439 //
One who through wisdom never perceives difference between the inner Self and <s>Brahman</s>,
one who maintains equanimity — that one bears the mark of <s>jīvanmukti</s>. // 440 //
When honored by the virtuous or tormented by the wicked,
like river streams into the ocean,
and are dissolved into pure being without producing any disturbance —
that <s>yati</s> (renunciant) is liberated. // 441 //
One into whom sense-objects directed by others enter

children.text: asti cen na sa vijñātabrahmabhāvo bahirmukhaḥ // 442 //
children.translated_text: if it does, then one has not truly known <s>Brahman</s>, being outward-facing. // 442 //
For one who has known the reality of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>saṃsāra</s> does not continue as before;
no, [for] through the knowledge of oneness with <s>Sat</s> (Being), <s>vāsanās</s> gradually weaken. // 443 //
If one objects that he continues in <s>saṃsāra</s> due to the momentum of prior <s>vāsanās</s> —
just so, for the wise, when <s>Brahman</s> — perfect bliss — is known. // 444 //
Even the activity of one extremely lustful is checked in the presence of his mother;
the <s>Śruti</s> declares his <s>prārabdha</s> (destiny begun) based on the observation of [residual] effects. // 445 //
For one devoted to <s>nididhyāsana</s> (deep meditation), external perceptions are observed;

children.text: phalodayaḥ kriyāpūrvo niṣkriyo na hi kutracit // 446 //
children.translated_text: the arising of fruits is preceded by action; there is never [fruit] without action. // 446 //
As long as there is experience of pleasure and the like, so long is <s>prārabdha</s> admitted;
is dissolved, like actions in a dream upon awakening. // 447 //
From the knowledge 'I am <s>Brahman</s>,' the <s>sañcita karma</s> (accumulated actions) acquired over hundreds of crores of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages)

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ svapnavelāyāṃ puṇyaṃ vā pāpam ulbaṇam &
suptotthitasya kiṃ tat syāt svargāya narakāya vā // 448 //
children.translated_text: upon waking, does that lead one to heaven or to hell? // 448 //
Whatever meritorious or extremely sinful deed was done during the state of dream —

children.text: svam asaṅgam udāsīnaṃ parijñāya nabho yathā &
na śliṣyati ca yat kiṃcit kadācid bhāvikarmabhiḥ // 449 //
children.translated_text: It never clings to anything through future actions. // 449 //
Knowing oneself to be unattached and indifferent, like space,
Likewise, the Self is not tainted by the properties of its limiting adjuncts due to contact with them. // 450 //
Space is not tainted by the odor of liquor due to its contact with a pot;
Without yielding its fruit — like an arrow released at a target. // 451 //
<s>Prārabdha karma</s> (karma already commenced) before the dawn of knowledge is not destroyed by knowledge,

children.text: na tiṣṭhati chinaty eva lakṣyaṃ vegena nirbharam // 452 //
children.translated_text: Does not stop afterward, but pierces the target with full force. // 452 //
An arrow released under the delusion that a cow is a tiger

children.text: prābdhaṃ balavattaraṃ khalu vidāṃ bhogena tasya kṣayaḥ

children.translated_text: The <s>sañcita</s> (accumulated) and <s>āgāmin</s> (future) karmas are dissolved by the fire of perfect knowledge.
But those who, having perceived the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and the Self, remain always established in that identity —

children.text: teṣāṃ tattritayaṃ nahi kvacid api brahmaiva te nirguṇam // 453 //
children.translated_text: For them, that triad [of karmas] does not exist anywhere; they are <s>Brahman</s> alone, without attributes. // 453 //
<s>Prārabdha</s> (commenced karma) is indeed most powerful for the wise; its exhaustion is through experience.
Devoid of identification with limiting adjuncts,
The talk of the existence of <s>prārabdha</s> is not appropriate,
Just as talk of the connection with dream-objects is not for one who is awake. // 454 //
For the sage who abides in the Self as the absolute <s>Brahman</s> alone,
Or the phenomenal world that serves the body,
Entertain the notions of 'I,' 'mine,' or 'this,'
But rather remains by himself in wakefulness. // 455 //
Indeed, one who has awakened does not, with regard to the illusory body
Nor is any clinging to that [illusory] world observed in him.
If there were continued engagement with false objects,
He would certainly not be regarded as freed from sleep. // 456 //
He has no desire to establish the reality of illusory objects,
Remains always as the Self and perceives nothing else.
Just as memory of objects seen in a dream [fades upon waking],
So too for the knower, regarding eating, evacuation, and the like. // 457 //
Similarly, one who abides in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>

children.text: karmaṇā nirmito dehaḥ prārabdhaṃ tasya kalpyatām &

children.translated_text: It is not proper to attribute it to the Self, which is beginningless; the Self was never fashioned by <s>karma</s>. // 458 //
The body was fashioned by <s>karma</s>; let <s>prārabdha</s> be attributed to that body.

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvata iti brūte śrutiramoghavāk &

children.translated_text: For one abiding as that Self, how can there be any attribution of <s>prārabdha</s>? // 459 //
"Unborn, eternal, everlasting" — thus declares the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture), whose words are infallible.

children.text: prārabdhaṃ sidhyati tadā yadā dehātmanā sthitiḥ &

children.translated_text: Since identification with the body is never desirable, <s>prārabdha</s> should therefore be relinquished. // 460 //
<s>Prārabdha</s> is valid only so long as one identifies with the body.
The attribution of <s>prārabdha</s> even to the body is indeed delusion,
For how can a superimposed thing have reality? How can an unreal thing have birth?
How can that which was never born have destruction? How can <s>prārabdha</s> exist for the unreal? // 461 //

children.text: tiṣṭhatyayaṃ kathaṃ deha iti śaṅkāvato jaḍān // 462 //
children.translated_text: Then how does this body continue to exist? — thus some dull-witted ones doubt. // 462 //
If through knowledge, the effects of ignorance, together with their root, are dissolved,
But not to teach the reality of the body and the like to the wise. // 463 //
To satisfy them from the external viewpoint, the scripture speaks of <s>prārabdha</s>,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 464 //
Absolutely full, without beginning or end, immeasurable, unchanging,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 465 //
A mass of existence, a mass of consciousness, eternal, a mass of bliss, actionless,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 466 //
Inward-facing, of one essence, complete, infinite, all-pervading,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 467 //
Nothing to be rejected, nothing to be taken up, nothing to be received, without support,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 468 //
Without attributes, without parts, subtle, without modification, without stain,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 469 //
Whose nature is indescribable, beyond the reach of mind and speech,
One alone, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — there is no multiplicity here whatsoever. // 470 //
Abundant in reality, self-established, pure, awakened, incomparable,
Who are peaceful, supremely self-controlled,
Having realized this supreme truth, at the end
Have attained the highest bliss through union with the Self. // 471 //
Those great ascetics who have cast off attachment and abandoned all enjoyments,
Whose nature is a mass of bliss,
Having dispelled the delusion fabricated by your own mind,
Become liberated, fulfilled, and awakened! // 472 //
May you too, having investigated this supreme truth of the Self,
Behold the truth of the Self with the eye of clear knowledge.
If it is properly perceived without doubt,
The meaning heard [from scripture] is never again subject to question. // 473 //
Through <s>samādhi</s> (meditation), with a truly steadied mind,
And in the attainment of the Self whose nature is truth, knowledge, and infinite bliss,
Scripture, reasoning, and the teacher's words are the means of knowledge,
And the inner experience established within oneself is also a means of knowledge. // 474 //
In the liberation from the bondage of one's own <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
Are known by oneself alone; another's knowledge of these is merely inferential. // 475 //
Bondage, liberation, satisfaction, anxiety, health, hunger, and the like
The wise person should cross over by one's own wisdom, favored by the Lord. // 476 //
The <s>gurus</s> (teachers) standing on the bank instruct, as do the scriptures;
The perfected one stands face to face, abiding in the Self as the Self, free from mental constructs. // 477 //
Having known by one's own experience one's own undivided Self,
<s>Brahman</s> alone is the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and the entire universe.
Abidance in the undivided reality is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);
The <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures) are the authority that <s>Brahman</s> is non-dual. // 478 //
This is the definitive pronouncement of <s>Vedānta</s>:
Having realized the supreme truth through reasoning about the Self,
With senses stilled and mind composed,
He became motionless somewhere, established in the Self. // 479 //
Thus, by the words of the <s>guru</s> and the authority of scripture,

children.text: kiṃcit kālaṃ samādhāya pare brahmaṇi mānasam &

children.translated_text: He arose and, from supreme bliss, spoke these words: // 480 //
Having absorbed the mind in the supreme <s>Brahman</s> for some time,
Through the realization of the identity of <s>Brahman</s> and the Self.

children.text: idaṃ na jāne 'py anidaṃ na jāne
children.translated_text: I know not 'this,' nor do I know 'not-this' —
What is this bliss, how much is it? It is boundless! // 481 //
The intellect has vanished, all activity has dissolved,

children.text: vācā vaktumaśakyam eva manasā mantuṃ na vā śakyate

children.translated_text: Cannot be expressed by speech, nor conceived by the mind.
My mind, like a hailstone dissolved in the ocean,
Having merged in even the minutest fraction of a fraction of it, is now blissful in its very nature. // 482 //
The glory of the ocean of supreme <s>Brahman</s>, filled with the flood of the nectar of one's own bliss,

children.text: kva gataṃ kena vā nītaṃ kutra līnamidaṃ jagat &
adhunaiva mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nāsti kiṃ mahadadbhutam // 483 //
children.translated_text: It was seen by me just now, yet now it does not exist — what a great wonder! // 483 //
Where has this world gone? By whom was it removed? Where has it dissolved?
In the great ocean of <s>Brahman</s>, filled with the nectar of undivided bliss! // 484 //
What is to be rejected? What is to be taken up? What is other? What is different?

children.text: na kiṃcid atra paśyāmi na śṛṇomi na vedmy aham &

children.translated_text: I exist as the Self alone, of the nature of eternal bliss, distinct [from all else]. // 485 //
I see nothing here, I hear nothing, I know nothing;
Free from all attachment, supremely good,
Whose very nature is the essence of eternal, non-dual bliss,
The infinite, the ever-boundless ocean of compassion! // 486 //
Salutations, salutations to you, O <s>Guru</s>, O great soul,
The weariness of the afflictions of worldly existence has been dispelled.
I have attained in an instant the imperishable abode of the Self,
Of undivided glory and bliss. // 487 //
By the fall of the dense moonlight of your gracious side-glance,
I am of the nature of eternal bliss! I am full — by your grace! // 488 //
Blessed am I! I have fulfilled my purpose! I am liberated from the grip of worldly existence!
I am serene, I am infinite, I am stainless, I am the most ancient. // 489 //
I am unattached, I am bodiless, I am without the subtle body, I am indestructible.
I am of the nature of pure consciousness, I am the absolute, I am ever auspicious (<s>Sadāśiva</s>). // 490 //
I am not the doer, I am not the enjoyer, I am changeless, I am actionless.
I am eternal, unbroken, actionless, limitless, unattached, of the nature of complete consciousness. // 491 //
I am indeed distinct from the seer, the hearer, the speaker, the doer, and the enjoyer.

children.text: nāhamidaṃ nāhamado 'py ubhayor avabhāsakaṃ paraṃ śuddham &

children.translated_text: Void of inside and outside, full — I am the non-dual <s>Brahman</s> itself. // 492 //
I am not 'this,' nor am I 'that' — I am the supreme, pure illuminator of both,
Of the one essence of eternal bliss, the truth — I am the non-dual <s>Brahman</s> itself. // 493 //
Incomparable, beginningless reality, far from the imaginations of 'you,' 'I,' 'this,' or 'that,'
I am the destroyer of the cities, I am the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Lord.
I am undivided consciousness, I am the witness of all,
I am without a lord, I am without ego, and without possessiveness. // 494 //
I am <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, I am the destroyer of <s>Naraka</s> (hell),
Being the Self of consciousness, the support of what is within and without.

children.text: bhoktā ca bhogyaṃ svayam eva sarvaṃ
children.translated_text: I am the enjoyer and the enjoyed, all of it myself —
Everything that was formerly seen as separate through the notion of 'this.' // 495 //
I alone am established in all beings,
Arise and dissolve through the agitation of the wind of <s>māyā</s>. // 496 //
In me, the ocean of undivided bliss, the manifold waves of the universe
By people, through the appearance of what is falsely attributed,
Just as divisions of time — <s>kalpas</s>, years, half-years,
Seasons, and the like — are [superimposed] upon the partless and unconditioned [time]. // 497 //
The states of gross and other [bodies] are superimposed upon me through delusion
Even when attributed by the deluded who are severely afflicted by defects.
The great flood of mirage-water does not moisten
A patch of barren, saline ground. // 498 //
That which is superimposed never truly corrupts the substratum,
Like the sun, I am distinct from what is illumined.
Like a mountain, I am eternally immovable;
Like the ocean, I am without shore. // 499 //
Like space, I am far from being tainted;

children.text: na me dehena saṃbandho megheneva vihāyasaḥ &

children.translated_text: How then can the properties of that [body] — waking, dreaming, and deep sleep — belong to me? // 500 //
I have no connection with the body, just as space has none with clouds.
It alone performs actions and enjoys their fruits.
It alone ages and dies — while I always
Remain immovable, like the <s>Kula</s> mountain (<s>Meru</s>). // 501 //
The limiting adjunct comes and the same goes;

children.text: na me pravṛttirna ca me nivṛttiḥ

children.translated_text: For I am ever of one nature, without parts.
One who is of a single nature, compact, without interval,

children.text: vyomeva pūrṇaḥ sa kathaṃ nu ceṣṭate // 502 //
children.translated_text: Full like space — how can such a one act? // 502 //
For me there is neither engagement nor withdrawal,
Without mind, without modification, without form —
How can they belong to me, who experiences undivided bliss?
The <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) indeed declares: 'It is untouched [by karma].' // 503 //
Merits and sins — for one without sense organs,

children.text: chāyayā spṛṣṭamuṣṇaṃ vā śītaṃ vā suṣṭhu duḥṣṭhu vā &
na spṛśaty eva yat kiṃcit puruṣaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam // 504 //
children.translated_text: Does not touch the person who is distinct from that [shadow]. // 504 //
Heat or cold, the pleasant or unpleasant — anything touched by a shadow
Unchanging, indifferent — as the properties of a house do not touch the lamp. // 505 //
The properties of what is witnessed do not touch the witness, who is distinct [from them],
Just as fire is not governed by what it burns,
Just as the rope has no connection with the object superimposed upon it,
So too am I, the immutable conscious Self. // 506 //
Just as the sun is a witness to actions,
Neither the enjoyer nor the cause of enjoyment,
Neither the seer nor the cause of seeing —
I am that Self, self-luminous, unlike anything else. // 507 //
I am neither the doer nor the cause of action,
The deluded attribute to the original, which is like the sun and actionless,
What belongs to the adjunct alone,
[Saying] 'I am the doer, I am the enjoyer, I am slain, alas!' // 508 //
When the limiting adjunct moves, the restlessness of the reflection [is attributed to the original];

children.text: jale vāpi sthale vāpi luṭhatveṣa jaḍātmakaḥ &
nāhaṃ vilipye taddharmair ghaṭadharmair nabho yathā // 509 //
children.translated_text: I am not stained by its properties, just as space is not by the properties of a pot. // 509 //
Let this inert [body] roll about in water or on land —
Inertness, bondage, liberation, and the like —
These are modifications of the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and do not exist in reality
In the Self, the supreme, absolute, non-dual <s>Brahman</s>. // 510 //
Agency, enjoyership, villainy, intoxication,

children.text: santu vikārāḥ prakṛterdaśadhā śatadhā sahasradhā vāpi &
kiṃ me 'saṅgacitastair na ghanaḥ kvacidambaraṃ spṛśati // 511 //
children.translated_text: What have they to do with me, the unattached consciousness? A cloud never touches the sky. // 511 //
Let there be ten, a hundred, or even a thousand modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s> —
Universe appears as a mere appearance in That.
Like space, subtle, without beginning or end —
I am that very non-dual <s>Brahman</s>! // 512 //
From the Unmanifest down to the gross [body], this entire
Of all forms, all-pervading, void of all,
Eternal, pure, immovable, free from mental constructs —
I am that very non-dual <s>Brahman</s>! // 513 //
The support of all, the illuminator of all things,
Of the nature of inner consciousness, inaccessible to thought,
Of the form of truth, knowledge, infinity, and bliss —
I am that very non-dual <s>Brahman</s>! // 514 //
In which all the particulars of <s>māyā</s> are negated,
I am without parts, I am without form.
I am free from mental constructs, I am eternal,
I am without support, I am non-dual. // 515 //
I am actionless, I am changeless,
I am pure undivided awareness alone, I am uninterrupted bliss. // 516 //
I am the Self of all, I am all, I transcend all, I am non-dual;
has been attained by me through the gracious magnificence of your compassion;
to the great-souled <s>Śrī Guru</s>, salutations,
salutations to you, and again salutations! // 517 //
This sovereignty and supreme dominion, this glory,
wandering, afflicted by the most intense sufferings day after day,
terrified by the tiger of ego — this one, with utmost compassion,
you have awakened from sleep and saved, O <s>Guru</s>! // 518 //
In the great dream, in the dense forest of birth, old age, and death created by <s>Māyā</s> (illusion),
which shines in the form of this universe — to you, O king of <s>Gurus</s>! // 519 //
Salutations to that one eternal reality; salutations to that indescribable effulgence of consciousness,
who had attained the bliss of the Self, who had realized the truth,
that lord of teachers, the great soul, with a delighted heart,
spoke again these supreme words: // 520 //
Beholding the excellent disciple who had bowed thus,
behold with the inner spiritual vision, with a tranquil mind, in all states;
is anything other than form seen anywhere by those who have eyes?
Likewise, for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> who abides in reality, what else is the domain of the intellect? // 521 //
The continuous stream of awareness of <s>Brahman</s> is the world; therefore, all is <s>Brahman</s> alone;
would delight in empty things?
When the greatly delightful moon is shining,
who would wish to look at a painted moon? // 522 //
What wise person, having abandoned that experience of the essence of supreme bliss,
any satisfaction nor any removal of sorrow;
therefore, satisfied with the experience of the essence of non-dual bliss,
abide happily, established in the true Self. // 523 //
Through the experience of unreal objects, there is neither
enjoying the bliss of oneself — spend your time thus, O great-minded one! // 524 //
Seeing only oneself everywhere, thinking of oneself as the non-dual,
conceptualization is like imagining a city in the sky;
through that non-dual, bliss-filled Self, always
having attained supreme peace, embrace silence. // 525 //
In the undivided awareness-Self, beyond all conceptual thought,
because the intellect is the cause of unreal imaginations and conceptual constructs;
for the great-souled knower of <s>Brahman</s>, who is <s>Brahman</s>-Self,
there is uninterrupted bliss of non-dual happiness. // 526 //
The state of silence is the supreme tranquility,
for one who has realized the nature of the Self and drinks the essence of one's own bliss. // 527 //
There is no supreme joy-producing excellence greater than silence born of the absence of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions),
the wise one, the sage who delights in the Self, may dwell as he pleases. // 528 //
Whether walking, standing, sitting, lying down, or in any other posture,
whose activity is not dependent on place, time, posture, direction, discipline,
or objects of contemplation and the like —
what rule or condition exists for the knowledge of oneself? // 529 //
For the great soul who has fully realized the truth,
Other than the proper functioning of the means of knowledge, through which the cognition of the object arises? // 530 //
What rule is required to know 'this is a pot'?

children.text: na deśaṃ nāpi kālaṃ na śuddhiṃ vāpyapekṣate // 531 //
children.translated_text: it does not require any [particular] place, time, or purification. // 531 //
This <s>Ātman</s> is eternally established and shines when the means of knowledge is present;
likewise, for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the realization 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' [requires nothing else]. // 532 //
'I am <s>Devadatta</s>' — this knowledge requires nothing else;
what could possibly illuminate that which is non-Self, unreal, and worthless? // 533 //
The entire world shines by whose effulgence, like the sun itself;
what could illuminate the knower by whom all these become meaningful? // 534 //
The <s>Vedas</s>, scriptures, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and all beings —
immeasurable, the experience of all;
having known It, freed from bondage,
this supreme among the supreme knowers of <s>Brahman</s> triumphs! // 535 //
This Self is self-luminous, of infinite power,
neither attached nor detached;
he always sports and rejoices in himself,
satisfied with the essence of uninterrupted bliss. // 536 //
He is neither distressed nor delighted by sense objects,

children.text: kṣudhāṃ dehavyathāṃ tyaktvā bālaḥ krīḍati vastuniḥ &
tathaiva vidvān ramate nirmamo nirahaṃ sukhī // 537 //
children.translated_text: so too the wise one revels — free from possessiveness, free from ego, happy. // 537 //
Just as a child plays with objects, having abandoned hunger and bodily pain,
dwelling freely without restraint, sleeping fearlessly in the cremation ground or forest,
clothing being the directions themselves, without washing or drying, the earth being the bed,

children.text: saṃcāro nigamāntavīthiṣu vidāṃ krīḍā pare brahmaṇi // 538 //
children.translated_text: wandering in the pathways of <s>Vedānta</s>, the sport of the wise is in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. // 538 //
Eating alms free from care and humiliation, drinking the waters of rivers,
he experiences all sense objects as they present themselves,
by the will of others, like a child — the knower of the Self,
who bears no distinguishing marks and is unattached to externals. // 539 //
Relying on this vehicle of the body,
or clothed in a skin, established in the expanse of consciousness,
like a madman, or like a child,
or like a ghost — he wanders on the earth. // 540 //
Whether sky-clad or robed,

children.text: svātmanaiva sadā tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sarvātmanā sthitaḥ // 541 //
children.translated_text: always content in his own Self, established as the Self of all. // 541 //
Free from desires, in the form of desirelessness, the sage moves about alone;
sometimes as a wanderer, sometimes gentle, sometimes adopting the conduct of a python,
sometimes honored, sometimes despised, sometimes unknown —
thus does the wise one move about, ever happy in supreme bliss. // 542 //
Sometimes appearing as a fool, sometimes as one of great royal splendor,
though ever satisfied, appearing not to eat; though peerless, seeing all as equal. // 543 //
Though possessionless, ever content; though without a helper, of great strength;
though embodied, yet bodiless; though limited, yet all-pervading. // 544 //
Though acting, yet not acting; though enjoying fruits, yet not an enjoyer;
is never touched by the pleasant or unpleasant, nor by the auspicious or inauspicious. // 545 //
This knower of <s>Brahman</s>, ever disembodied and tranquil,

children.text: sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca śubhāśubhe ca &
children.translated_text: there is happiness and sorrow, the auspicious and the inauspicious;
for the sage of the eternal Self, whose bondage has been destroyed —
whence comes the auspicious, the inauspicious, or any result? // 546 //
For one who identifies with the gross body and the like,
'eclipsed' — through delusion indeed, not knowing the true nature of the thing. // 547 //
Though the sun is not actually swallowed by darkness, people say it is
is seen by the deluded as if embodied, due to the appearance of a body. // 548 //
Likewise, the supreme knower of <s>Brahman</s>, who is liberated from the bonds of body and the like,

children.text: ahirnirlvayanīṃ vāyaṃ muktvā dehaṃ tu tiṣṭhati &

children.translated_text: moved here and there somewhat by the vital breath. // 549 //
Like a snake that has cast off its old skin, he remains, shedding the body,
so too the body is carried by fate to its destined experiences in due time. // 550 //
Just as a piece of wood is carried by a current to low and high ground,
the liberated one's body moves among experiences like a worldly person;
but the perfected one himself dwells silently as a witness,
like the hub of a wheel, free from all imagined constructs. // 551 //
Through the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) determined by <s>prārabdha karma</s> (karma already set in motion),
nor withdraws them, remaining in the state of mere witnessing;
nor does he even slightly regard the fruit of actions,
his mind being intoxicated with drinking the concentrated essence of his own bliss. // 552 //
He neither directs the senses toward objects
he is <s>Śiva</s> (the auspicious one) himself, directly — this supreme knower of <s>Brahman</s>. // 553 //
He who, abandoning the movement toward the defined and the undefined, abides in the pure Self alone —

children.text: jīvann eva sadā muktaḥ kṛtārtho brahmavittamaḥ &

children.translated_text: upon the destruction of the limiting adjuncts, being <s>Brahman</s> itself, merges into non-dual <s>Brahman</s>. // 554 //
Even while living, always liberated, having fulfilled his purpose, the supreme knower of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: śailūṣo veṣasadbhāvā- bhāvayoś ca yathā pumān &
tathaiva brahmavic chreṣṭhaḥ sadā brahmaiva nāparaḥ // 555 //
children.translated_text: so too the supreme knower of <s>Brahman</s> is always <s>Brahman</s> alone, and nothing else. // 555 //
Just as an actor is a man whether in costume or out of it,

children.text: yatra kvāpi viśīrṇaṃ satparṇam iva taror vapuḥ patatāt &
brahmībhūtasya yateḥ prāg eva taccidagninā dagdham // 556 //
children.translated_text: for one who has become <s>Brahman</s>, the renunciant's [body] has already been consumed by the fire of consciousness. // 556 //
Let the body fall anywhere, like a withered leaf from a tree;
always in the form of the full, non-dual, blissful Self,
there is no waiting for the proper place or time
for the casting off of this mass of skin, flesh, and excrement. // 557 //
For the sage who abides in <s>Brahman</s>, the real Self,

children.text: dehasya mokṣo no mokṣo na daṇḍasya kamaṇḍaloḥ &

children.translated_text: liberation is the untying of the knot of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the heart — that is true liberation. // 558 //
Liberation is not of the body, nor of the staff, nor of the water-pot;

children.text: parṇaṃ patati cettena taroḥ kiṃ nu śubhāśubham // 559 //
children.translated_text: if a leaf falls, what good or ill comes to the tree thereby? // 559 //
Whether in a canal, or in a river, or in a holy site, or at a crossroads,
so is the destruction of the body, senses, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), and intellect;
but not of the Self itself, whose nature is the eternal Self,
of the form of bliss — like the tree, it stands. // 560 //
Like the destruction of a leaf, a flower, or a fruit,
being restated, the scriptures speak of the destruction of only that which pertains to the limiting adjuncts. // 561 //
'A mass of consciousness' — this definition of the <s>Ātman</s>, indicating reality,
declares the indestructibility of the <s>Ātman</s> even while the changing modifications perish. // 562 //
'Indestructible indeed is this Self' — thus the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture)

children.text: dagdhā bhavanti hi mṛd eva yathā tathaiva &
children.translated_text: when burned, become merely earth — so too,
the body, senses, vital airs, mind, and all that is perceived,
when burned by the fire of knowledge, attains the state of the supreme Self. // 563 //
Just as stones, trees, grass, grain, husks, and the like,
so too all that is perceived dissolves into <s>Brahman</s>. // 564 //
Just as darkness, being different [from light], dissolves in the radiance of the sun,

children.text: ghaṭe naṣṭe yathā vyoma vyomaiva bhavati sphuṭam &

children.translated_text: so too when the limiting adjuncts dissolve, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> himself becomes <s>Brahman</s> alone. // 565 //
Just as when a pot is destroyed, the space [within it] becomes clearly just space,

children.text: kṣīraṃ kṣīre yathā kṣiptaṃ tailaṃ taile jalaṃ jale &

children.translated_text: becomes united and attains oneness — so too the sage, the knower of the Self, [merges] into the Self. // 566 //
Just as milk poured into milk, oil into oil, water into water,
having reached the state of <s>Brahman</s>, this renunciant does not return again. // 567 //
Thus, attaining disembodied liberation (<s>videha-kaivalya</s>), the undivided state of pure existence,
since he has become <s>Brahman</s>, whence could there be any arising from <s>Brahman</s>? // 568 //
For him whose body of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the like has been burned by the knowledge of the identity of the real Self,

children.text: māyākḷptau bandhamokṣau na staḥ svātmani vastutaḥ &

children.translated_text: just as the appearance and disappearance of a snake [do not truly exist] in the inactive rope. // 569 //
Bondage and liberation, fashioned by <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), do not truly exist in the Self;
Bondage and liberation are spoken of in terms of the existence and non-existence of the covering;
but there is no covering of <s>Brahman</s> whatsoever — being uncovered due to the absence of anything else;

children.text: yady asty advaitahāniḥ syād dvaitaṃ no sahate śrutiḥ // 570 //
children.translated_text: if there were, there would be the loss of non-duality — the <s>Śruti</s> does not tolerate duality. // 570 //
by the deluded, as qualities of the intellect;
just as the covering of sight caused by a cloud [is attributed] to the sun —
for this imperishable [Self] is non-dual, unattached consciousness. // 571 //
Both bondage and liberation are falsely attributed to reality

children.text: astīti pratyayo yaśca yaśca nāstīti vastuni &
buddher eva guṇāvetau na tu nityasya vastunaḥ // 572 //
children.translated_text: these are both qualities of the intellect alone, not of the eternal reality. // 572 //
The notion 'it exists' and the notion 'it does not exist' regarding reality —

children.text: atastau māyayā kḷptau bandhamokṣau na cātmani &
children.translated_text: Therefore, both bondage and liberation are fashioned by <s>Māyā</s>, not in the <s>Ātman</s>;
in the partless, actionless, tranquil, faultless, untainted,
non-dual, supreme reality, like space — whence any imagining? // 573 //

children.text: na nirodho na cotpattirna baddho na ca sādhakaḥ &
na mumukṣurna vai mukta ityeṣā paramārthatā // 574 //
children.translated_text: neither a seeker of liberation nor indeed one liberated — this is the ultimate truth. // 574 //
There is neither cessation nor origination, neither one bound nor a practitioner,
has been shown to you by me today;
regarding you as my own son repeatedly — one free from the taint of the age of <s>Kali</s>,
whose intellect is freed from desire, a seeker of liberation. // 575 //
This supreme, most secret [teaching], the established conclusion within all the crests of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Upaniṣads</s>),

children.text: iti śrutvā guror vākyaṃ praśrayeṇa kṛtānatiḥ &

children.translated_text: he, with the teacher's permission, departed, freed from all bondage. // 576 //
Having heard the words of the <s>Guru</s>, having bowed with reverence,
wandered unceasingly, purifying the entire earth. // 577 //
The <s>Guru</s> himself, his mind immersed in the ocean of eternal bliss,
has been determined, for the easy understanding of seekers of liberation. // 578 //
Thus, through this dialogue between the teacher and the disciple, the nature of the Self
who have properly removed all defects of the mind,
who are detached from worldly pleasures, whose minds are tranquil,
who delight in the <s>Śruti</s> (scripture) — those <s>yatis</s> (renunciants) and seekers of liberation [attain the goal]. // 579 //
May those who cherish this beneficial teaching,
wandering in the desert through delusion, thirsting for water,
this speech of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, bestowing <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation), triumphs,
pointing out the very near ocean of nectar — the bliss-giving, non-dual <s>Brahman</s>! // 580 //
For those afflicted by the burning pain produced by the scorching rays of the sun of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
Thus ends the <s>Vivekacūḍāmaṇi</s>, composed by <s>Śaṅkarācārya</s>.
<s>Oṃ tat sat</s>.
